texts.li: [age0] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with no people near, has come to the gate as the light goes and asks {A_nameDef} for a place by the fire for the night. {X_pronoun} carries nothing but a stick and a skin of water, and doesn't seem tired at all.

[age1] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} on the long road, has knocked at the gate and asks {A_nameDef} for a bed and a bowl for one night, in the name of whatever the colony holds holy. The dust on {X_possessive} cloak is from no road anyone here knows.

[age2] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with a battered pack and a coat too thin for the season, is waiting at the gate. {X_pronoun} asks {A_nameDef} for a roof for the night and a plate of whatever is going, and offers nothing for it but thanks.

[age3] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} in a scuffed suit with no ship and no beacon, walked in out of the wilds and asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for a night. {X_possessive} suit's readings are all zeroes, which shouldn't be possible.
A {TALE} named {X_nameDef} is standing at the gate with {X_possessive} hood down and asks {A_nameDef}, quite simply, whether there is room for one more tonight.
[storm] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE}, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night. The sky has been heavy all afternoon, and {X_pronoun} glances at it the way someone glances at an old friend.
[harvest] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with seeds caught in the hem of {X_possessive} coat, asks {A_nameDef} for a bed for the night and says the colony's fields look thirsty.
[hunt] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} who walks without a sound, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night. The dogs, for once, have not barked at all.
[healing] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with a satchel that smells of clean herbs, asks {A_nameDef} for a bed for the night and asks after the colony's sick before anything else.
[way] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} who seems to have walked every road there is, asks {A_nameDef} for a corner for the night and the news from these parts.
[hearth] {X_nameDef}, an old {TALE} with ember-bright eyes and a shawl that smells of smoke, asks {A_nameDef} for a bowl and a corner by the fire.
[dead] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} in gray who knows the names on the colony's graves without being told, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night.
[night] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} who only came out of the trees at dusk, asks {A_nameDef} for a bed and says {X_pronoun} sleeps lightly.
[wild] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with leaves in {X_possessive} hair and mud to the knee, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night, and the birds come down to the wall to look.
[waters] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} whose clothes are wet though it hasn't rained for days, asks {A_nameDef} for a dry corner for the night.
[war] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with an old soldier's way of standing, asks {A_nameDef} for a bed for the night and doesn't take {X_possessive} eyes off the colony's walls.
[craft] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with burn scars on both hands, asks {A_nameDef} for a bed for the night and looks over the colony's tools with interest.
[machine] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} who talks a little too evenly, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night and somehow knows the colony's power is low.
[void] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} whose shadow seems a little late to follow, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night. It's hard to remember {X_possessive} face afterwards.
[ennu,rememberskind] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE}, is at the gate again, or someone very like the last one. {X_pronoun} smiles at {A_nameDef} as if they were old friends, and asks for a bed for the night.

[ennu,rememberscold] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE}, stands at the gate and asks {A_nameDef} for shelter. {X_pronoun} looks at the colony's door for a long moment before knocking, as if remembering how it was answered once.
[ennu,remembersharm] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE} with an old bruise on {X_possessive} cheek, asks {A_nameDef} for shelter for the night. Nobody here can say why the bruise looks so familiar.
[ennu,remembers] {X_nameDef}, a {TALE}, asks {A_nameDef} for a place for the night, and already seems to know where the well is.

li.label: Give {X_objective} a bed and a place at the table
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} brings {X_nameDef} in, and the colony finds the {TALE} a bed for the night and a place at the table.

li.label: Turn {X_objective} away
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} there is no room here. The {TALE} only nods, and turns back down the road.

li.label: Let {X_objective} sleep by the gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} may sleep outside by the gate tonight. No bed, no table, but no one will move {X_objective} on.

li.label: sat near the great beast
li.description: I sat near it while it grazed, and for a while nothing hurt.

li.label: touched its horn
li.description: It let me come right up close and touch its horn. It was warm.

li.label: a strange peace
li.description: The great white beast went its way and nobody raised a hand to it. Something has been quieter since.

li.label: a nightmare under the moon
li.description: I woke in the night from a dream I can't shake. The moon was very bright.

ColonyCouncil.SharedMemoryDef.label: saw a god come
ColonyCouncil.SharedMemoryDef.description: They were there when a god came to the colony, or something that might have been one. People who saw that together bring it up for years.

ColonyCouncil.DeedDef.label: was kind to a stranger who was more
ColonyCouncil.DeedDef.text: was kindest to the {DETAIL} who came to the gate

ColonyCouncil.DeedDef.label: struck the stranger at the gate
ColonyCouncil.DeedDef.text: struck the {DETAIL} who came to the gate
